observations: Photo 0 shows a black and silver electronic music module with 'EDIROL STUDIO Canvas SD-80' printed on the front and top.
The front panel has a blue LCD screen, a large knob, several buttons, and ports including MIDI and power.
Photo 1 is a similar front view, showing the same branding and controls, with the screen displaying 'PART10: C.H. Pad'.
Photo 2 is a close-up of the front panel, clearly showing the brand 'EDIROL', model 'STUDIO Canvas SD-80', and the screen displaying 'H01: D.L. Pad'.
The unit appears to be in used condition with some visible wear on the metal casing.
The seller's text mentions 'Roland', but no Roland branding is visible in the photos.

claims.claim: This is an Edirol SD-80 Studio Canvas 128-Voice USB Sound Module
claims.evidence: The brand and model are clearly visible on the front and top panels in all three photos.
The seller mentions Roland, but no Roland branding is visible in the photos. Edirol was a brand under Roland, but this cannot be confirmed from the images alone.
Visible wear on the metal casing in photo 0 and photo 1 indicates use.
Text below the screen in photo 2 reads '128 VOICES 32 PARTS 1050 INSTRUMENTS and 30 DRUM SETS'.

risks.risk: The unit may not power on or function properly
risks.proof: A video showing the unit powering on, displaying menus, and producing sound through a speaker or headphones.

risks.risk: The USB functionality may be faulty
risks.proof: A video showing the unit connected to a computer, recognized by the OS, and being used in a DAW.

risks.risk: The screen may be cracked or have dead pixels
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the screen showing all segments lit and no cracks or damage.
risks.if_unproven: priced as screen may be damaged

risks.risk: The unit may have internal damage or missing parts
risks.proof: A video showing the unit being opened (if safe) or a detailed inspection of all ports and connectors.
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly missing parts or damaged internally

proof_requests: A video showing the unit powering on and producing sound.
A video showing the unit connected to a computer via USB and recognized by the system.
A close-up photo of the screen showing no damage or dead pixels.
A photo or video showing all ports and connectors in good condition.
response.reason: The identity is confirmed as an Edirol SD-80, but critical functional risks (power, USB, sound output) cannot be verified from the photos alone. The unit must be proven to work before pricing can be determined.
